properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-09-27: "what happens if I dumped a bunch of documents in a new folder and wanted to run ingest_corpus_step? Isn't that done on this machine? Same with adopt skill - if I went to a codebase and said, run /adopt on it, yes, the remote reflow2 mcp serves the skill, but the work is done here on this machine??"

HE IS RIGHT, and the tools already say so:
- ingest_corpus_step: "YOU walk the directory and read the files — reflow2 performs no file I/O". The agent reads the documents here and sends their text; the server extracts nothing from disk. flo2's gateway refuses it on a wrong reason (flo2's fact:only-wall-check-of-the-machine-side-tools-reads-files-itself-2026-09-27).
- /adopt: the skill is served; the agent reads the codebase here with its own tools and writes the design through ordinary tools that are served remotely. Only its file-registration steps (link_artifact, coverage_report, reconcile_artifacts) are refused by flo2 today, and all three take their evidence from the caller.
- The same holds for reconcile_dependencies, link_artifact with a checksum, set_artifact_checksum(s), reconcile_artifacts with `observed`, coverage_report with `observed`.
- The one exception is wall_check, which walks the registered files' imports itself and runs a Python instrument over them.

THE IDEA: make "the caller brings the content" the rule for every tool that needs a file, and give wall_check the same shape (the caller sends each registered file's imports), so a design on a server loses nothing a local one has except what reads another design by path.

WHAT IT CHANGES, recorded beside it:
- The local client (combined position 7, epoch:planned-local-files-are-measured-for-a-remote-design) stops being the ONLY route for these tools and becomes the MEASURED route: a checksum the agent computes is `asserted` (its word), one the client takes is measured. That difference stays real, and the design already records it. DISTINCT FROM that epoch: it is about the client doing the measuring; this is about which tools need the client at all.
- For ingest there is no cost difference between local and remote: the model has to read every document to extract a design either way. For checksums, an agent running sha256sum is cheap; for a large tree the client does it without the model in the loop.
- wall_check reshaped would need the import graph from the caller, which today only the Python instrument computes. That is the one piece of real work.

Noticed, not claimed as a relation: this sits between req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url (whose point 3 is the client measuring files) and flo2's group-1 requirement. It narrows what the local client has to be for, and does not replace it.
properties.name: OPEN — the agent does the file work on the person's machine anyway: should every tool that needs a file take it from the caller, so a design on a server loses only what must run code over the files?
properties.no_relation_note: Searched reflow2's design for remote designs, local files, adopt and ingest. Nearest: epoch:planned-local-files-are-measured-for-a-remote-design and req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url (the client measuring files, which this idea narrows but does not duplicate, block or obsolete), dec:idea-a-repo-that-holds-its-design-moves-it-to-a-remote-server-once (about moving a design, not about which side reads files), fact:an-agent-opened-in-a-moved-designs-folder-is-served-the-frozen-store-2026-09-27 (a different failure). No relation in the vocabulary is honestly true of any of them; the connection is stated in the text instead.
